svg.aria-label: From a Python function to GPU code. jax.jit traces the Python function with abstract shapes and dtypes into a jaxpr, which is lowered to StableHLO. The XLA GPU compiler runs passes like CSE, fusion and buffer assignment, and fusion turns several ops such as a mul, an add and a tanh into one kernel. What it emits is kernels plus cuBLAS, cuDNN and NCCL calls, which the runtime runs as thunks and CUDA graphs on streams on the V100. Compilation happens once per shape, cached in memory keyed by shape and on disk when compiling takes about a second or more. The XLA flags from the post are on a note, the latency hiding scheduler on, small all-reduces merged, Triton needing compute capability 8.0 where the V100 is 7.0, and fast min/max skipping NaNs.
